sections.h2: St. Joseph County at a glance
sections.html:
Up in north central Indiana against the Michigan border, St. Joseph County has South Bend as its seat and biggest city, with Mishawaka second. Settlers organized it in 1830, and the river that crosses it gives the county its name. Its area is 461 square miles, and it belongs to the Michiana region.

The 2020 census found 272,912 people, and the July 2025 estimate of 272,861 shows almost no change. Owners live in about 69% of homes, valued at a median $192,800 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. The county has 119,768 housing units and 611 building permits were issued in 2025. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,291 a month and owners without one pay $479. Median gross rent is $1,062, and median household income is $66,868.

Those are countywide medians. Your bill turns on the assessment for your own parcel. The assessor values each parcel, the treasurer collects, and an Indiana bill stacks county, city and school levies.

A single bill arrives with both installments. Parcels that stay delinquent can be offered at a county tax sale. If you intend to sell, request a payoff figure from the treasurer before settling on a closing date.

The St. Joseph County Assessor, in the County-City Building, sets a value for every parcel. If you think yours is wrong, Indiana's Form 130 starts an appeal. In order:

  • File by June 15. When the notice of assessment went out before May 1, the date is June 15 of the assessment year. If not, it is June 15 of the year the treasurer mails the bill.
  • Use one petition per parcel.
  • The county board that hears these cases, called the PTABOA, has 180 days from filing to hold a hearing and must give at least 30 days' notice.
  • Unhappy with the ruling? Form 131 takes the case to the Indiana Board of Tax Review. That route is also open if 180 days pass without a PTABOA decision.
  • Skipping the hearing without an approved continuance or a timely withdrawal can cost $50.

The existing assessment starts out presumed correct. Where it jumped more than 5% from the previous date, the assessor must prove the number, unless the jump comes from improvements or a change in use.

Values lurched in recent years. Nearly 14,000 owners appealed in 2025. For 2026 the assessor reported an average countywide drop of 4%, with about 86% of the county landing on a lower value, and appeals were expected to fall well below the earlier count.

The office changed its method too. Long-time owners in areas such as Notre Dame and New Carlisle now form their own submarkets, so they are not measured against new construction. Land is valued by square footage instead of lot type, and a 20/80 rule puts 20% of value on land and 80% on improvements.

A five-acre lot that an owner bought for $9,000 in 2012 had its land value jump from $14,900 to $57,700. After an appeal the assessor brought it down to nearly $11,000. Appeals work best when the number on the notice conflicts with the facts about the property.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or an open appeal
sections.html:
At closing the title company works out what you owe and takes it out of your proceeds. How the current-year bill is split with the buyer comes from the purchase agreement, so ask the title company to show you the math before you sign.

  • Call the treasurer's office and ask whether any installment is unpaid.
  • Read the assessed value on your notice and decide if an appeal is still possible.
  • Expect the title search to find liens and open permits, and ask about them yourself first.
  • Put your Form 11 notice and tax bills in the closing folder.

We buy houses in St. Joseph County as-is, even with back taxes, tenants or needed repairs. The title company takes care of title and recording, and you decide whether to take the offer.

Because values moved so much between 2025 and 2026, a notice you set aside last year may now be off in the opposite direction. Anyone planning to sell soon gains from a lower assessment, since it lowers a buyer's carrying costs, and a higher one can be worth contesting before the house is listed. The assessor's office has held public sessions at local libraries before new notices, and those meetings are a place to ask how the submarkets were drawn.

Open the notice the day it arrives. The appeal period runs to a fixed date, and an owner who lets June 15 slide loses the simplest way to fix an error.

• Value too high or a wrong description of the house: the county assessor, through Form 130.
  • Balance, installments and penalties: the county treasurer.
  • A hearing on your appeal: the PTABOA, which meets after you file.
  • A result you dispute: the Indiana Board of Tax Review, with Form 131.

Sending a question to the wrong office costs days, and the June 15 date does not move. When in doubt, begin with the assessor for anything about value and the treasurer for anything about money owed. Both can tell you which form or payoff letter you need and where to deliver it, and you can ask either one to confirm in writing what you were told by phone.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
A little preparation shortens the process, and most of it takes one phone call to the county.

  1. Locate your last tax bill and your Form 11 notice.
  2. Ask the treasurer whether both installments for the year are paid, and request a payoff if anything is open.
  3. Check whether an appeal you filed is still pending, since a pending appeal is worth mentioning to the title company.
  4. List any tenants, liens or repairs the buyer should know about.
  5. Choose the closing date that fits your plans, then confirm it with the title company.

Selling does not require every item to be tidy. A cash buyer can work with back taxes, an unfinished repair or an unresolved appeal, because the title company settles balances at the table. The point of the list is to avoid surprises, which cost sellers more than the underlying problems do.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in St. Joseph County, Indiana?
faqs.a: Half is due in May and half on November 10, and one bill covers both. The 2026 spring date was May 11.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying St. Joseph County property tax late?
faqs.a: Pay within 30 days of the due date, with no back taxes owed, and the penalty is 5%. If tax and penalty remain unpaid after 30 days, it becomes 10%.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my St. Joseph County assessment?
faqs.a: Send Indiana Form 130 to the county assessor, one per parcel, by June 15 of the right year. A PTABOA hearing must follow within 180 days.

faqs.q: Who values my property in St. Joseph County?
faqs.a: The county assessor, in the County-City Building. The county treasurer handles collection.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in St. Joseph County with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. At closing the title company pays the balance from your proceeds, so get a payoff figure from the treasurer first.
